name: Code-Triggered Upgrades in Los Angeles Kitchen Remodel Permits

mainEntity.name: What specific upgrades usually become mandatory when pulling permits for a kitchen remodel in older Los Angeles County homes?
mainEntity.text: What specific upgrades usually become mandatory when pulling permits for a kitchen remodel in older Los Angeles County homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners are often surprised by “extra” work required once they decide to permit a kitchen remodel in an older Los Angeles County home. Building and electrical codes tie certain health and safety features to permitted work, so inspectors commonly require more than just new cabinets and finishes. In the kitchen itself, expect to upgrade outlets to GFCI and often AFCI protection, add required small-appliance and dedicated circuits for major appliances, and ensure proper range hood ventilation to the exterior. If walls are opened, inspectors may require updating wiring, boxes, and sometimes insulation. Beyond the kitchen, common mandatory upgrades include bringing smoke and carbon monoxide detectors up to current standards, securing the water heater with proper seismic strapping, and confirming that any new or altered glazing in hazardous locations (near doors or floors) is safety glass. In some cases, plumbing upgrades (such as replacing severely corroded galvanized supply lines) may be required if exposed and clearly deficient. These items add to the project budget but improve safety and resale value. When budgeting, ask your contractor what code-triggered upgrades are typical in your jurisdiction and how they will handle them in the proposal, so you are not caught off guard at inspection time.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permitted kitchen remodels in older Los Angeles homes often trigger mandatory upgrades like GFCI/AFCI protection, dedicated appliance circuits, hardwired smoke/CO detectors, seismic strapping for the water heater, and sometimes plumbing, ventilation, and safety glazing updates. These code-driven items add cost but are required for final inspection.
